title: JBPA Management Requirements Matrix
purpose: Preserve current MCP-driven onboarding, the minimal management bootstrap, file/profile/group relationships, agreed baseline behavior and deferred upgrades. This is planning, not a runtime implementation or deployment claim.

scopeMeaning.REQUIRES_QUALIFICATION: Do not offer until explicitly implemented and qualified
scopeMeaning.SKILL_SECURITY_FINAL_DEFERRED: Skill-specific security: final selected implementation phase, only on explicit request; required before production access

requirements.contract: Customer runs the installer locally on the initially bare management VM. It resolves required runtime parameters, deploys NGINX/API/PostgreSQL/worker and verifies management readiness. Jitterbit project/APIM/MCP is configured afterwards, followed by MCP-driven target onboarding.
requirements.acceptance: Management service can be reached through authenticated Jitterbit MCP before target credentials are collected.

requirements.contract: The AI uses Jitterbit MCP tools to fetch a trusted setup guide/options, prompt for host mappings, persist a validated plan and request execution. Local shell access, TTY forwarding and an AI installer adapter are not onboarding dependencies.
requirements.acceptance: Complete multi-host onboarding through MCP without granting the AI a management-host shell.

requirements.contract: Backend schemas, field rules, file IDs, profile revisions and resumable setup state are authoritative. Markdown explains the same rules to the AI; it does not implement or override them.
requirements.acceptance: Stale/incorrect AI answers or guide content cannot bypass server validation.

requirements.contract: Return versioned Markdown instructions and a machine-readable field/options contract through a scoped API/MCP response. The AI asks the customer for missing non-secret fields and calls setup tools with answers/references.
requirements.acceptance: Partial answers resume the same setup; choices use current IDs; no terminal prompt is needed.

requirements.contract: Capture tokens and secret files through a private authenticated upload/form or secret reference. The AI receives file/profile IDs and readiness, not private-key/token contents. Existing pre-staged files may be selected. Native MCP elicitation is optional only after capability/secret handling verification.
requirements.acceptance: No secrets appear in tool arguments/results, transcripts generated by the adapter, job payloads or diagnostic logs.

requirements.contract: Generate schema-valid inventory, registration credentials and management settings from MCP-collected selections. Customer stages existing files or uploads them through the authenticated Jitterbit file-transfer route; no manual JSON/YAML editing.
requirements.acceptance: Customer completes setup without creating or editing JSON/YAML/Compose.

requirements.contract: Persist setup stages, answers, profile revisions and per-host outcomes. Re-running preserves existing valid files and installed PA identity unless replacement/mutation is explicitly selected.
requirements.acceptance: Recover an interrupted setup and repeat a successful one without reinstall or credential overwrite.

requirements.contract: Show the complete per-host plan, selected profile/file IDs, groups, releases and intended actions. A confirmed executeSetup call creates durable work from that saved plan; prepareTarget remains file staging only.
requirements.acceptance: Execution binds a validated plan revision; subsequent edits cannot silently redirect queued jobs.

requirements.contract: Management stack uses its dedicated Linux/container host. Targets already exist and are reachable. Git checkout alone does not provision VMs.
requirements.acceptance: Fail with an actionable prerequisite report when infrastructure/access is absent.

requirements.contract: A guided cloud template or managed hosting can remove provisioning tasks for infrastructure-inexperienced customers. Provider, scope, authentication and costs are unresolved; no deployment is authorized here.
requirements.acceptance: Select and qualify a concrete provider/profile before offering automated provisioning.

requirements.contract: Allow pre-staged private setup-input files and authenticated uploaded files, indexed into a common typed registry. Publish required file roles and generated fields per selected feature; exclude local inputs from Git.
requirements.acceptance: Missing required files block the affected feature before target changes.

requirements.contract: Scan ssh/ and allowed profile subdirectories. Identify supported private keys, public keys and known_hosts by validated content/type; do not trust filename extensions alone. Show all candidates with stable IDs and safe metadata.
requirements.acceptance: Four staged private keys produce four visible candidates; public/invalid files are identified separately and are not misrepresented as login keys.

requirements.contract: Ask which private key/access profile and known-host record applies to each target. Do not infer mappings from filenames. Offer an explicit reuse choice across hosts.
requirements.acceptance: Four hosts can select four different keys or explicitly share a key; saved mappings survive restart.

requirements.contract: List TLS server certificates/keys/chains, CA certificates and qualified enterprise identity files in separate typed menus. Display filenames, public fingerprints/subjects, expiry and usability without content exposure.
requirements.acceptance: SSH, server-TLS, trust-CA and client-TLS roles cannot be accidentally substituted.

requirements.contract: Only accept permitted regular files under declared input roots or approved secret-provider references. Reject unsafe links/path escape and ambiguous/unsupported inputs.
requirements.acceptance: No selected file escapes the approved input root; invalid candidates show an actionable reason.

requirements.contract: Check ownership/mode and required key/certificate pairings. Pin the selected file/profile revision and revalidate if content changes before execution. Secret directories default to 0700 and private keys/credential documents to 0600, with ownership restricted to the executing identity; public trust material follows its declared profile.
requirements.acceptance: Changed/replaced keys or invalid certificate pairings invalidate readiness and require revalidation.

requirements.contract: Keep protected profiles/secret files outside Git and release images, or use an external secret manager. Only permitted components receive their secrets. Customer input files are not deleted automatically.
requirements.acceptance: Worker gets target keys/registration references; NGINX gets management TLS keys; inventory/jobs expose references only.

requirements.contract: Build target-specific credentials.json from the selected registration profile and target naming policy; validate schema, atomically stage and restrict permissions.
requirements.acceptance: Generated target file has required fields and correct permissions; no manual customer copying is necessary.

requirements.contract: Management login private keys stay on the management host. Only necessary target configuration and separately selected integration identities/certificates go to the target.
requirements.acceptance: Remote staging never transfers the management-to-target login private key.

requirements.contract: Prompt for host count, or derive it from a supplied inventory and confirm it. Support adding/removing targets before execution and onboarding more hosts later.
requirements.acceptance: One-host and four-host setup iterate the correct number of targets and remain editable.

requirements.contract: Collect target name, reachable private IP/hostname, SSH username, access profile, registration profile/group, name/prefix, release and selected optional features for every host.
requirements.acceptance: Each host has an explicit complete mapping; selections do not leak from a previous host.

requirements.contract: Offer apply-to-all defaults for username, registration group, release and optional features; ask for per-host overrides and show final assignments.
requirements.acceptance: Shared defaults reduce questions without silently assigning the wrong credentials/group.

requirements.requirement: SSH keys and pinned host identity
requirements.contract: Current caller requires private-key authentication, a pinned known_hosts file and passwordless sudo. Verify that the selected key authenticates the selected username on the specific host.
requirements.acceptance: Wrong key/user, unverified fingerprint and missing sudo fail before lifecycle mutation.

requirements.requirement: SSH password and other access choices
requirements.contract: Password login, passphrase-unlock flows, SSH certificates, bastions and alternate credential sources are explicit capability choices; current caller must not claim them as supported.
requirements.acceptance: Only implemented/qualified methods are selectable; no secret is passed through argv or AI-visible values.

requirements.contract: Aliases for the same VM share one canonical identity, mutation owner and lock across profiles, groups, setup jobs and lifecycle jobs.
requirements.acceptance: Aliases and changed group context cannot create concurrent mutations on the same VM.

requirements.contract: Validate all host mappings first and show individual readiness. Bound concurrency; preserve per-host jobs/results and isolate failures. Only ready explicitly selected hosts execute.
requirements.acceptance: One failed host does not hide other outcomes or cause blind retry; concurrency stays within configured limits.

requirements.contract: Use existing SSH for delivery, diagnostics and remote execution. Management API/database/HTTPS remain on the dedicated management host.
requirements.acceptance: No extra PA-host service or listener is introduced.

requirements.contract: Store reusable named profiles with cloud/region, organization/environment context where known, group ID, token reference, naming policy and revision. Allow different profiles per host.
requirements.acceptance: Four hosts can map to different permitted agent groups without duplicating token values in inventory.

requirements.contract: Allow the customer to select another authorized group/profile during setup or later via terminal/AI/MCP. Context filters discovery and future choices; it does not grant permissions.
requirements.acceptance: Switch group A to B and list only permitted targets/profiles; already submitted jobs retain their recorded context.

requirements.requirement: Create or update a group profile
requirements.contract: Guide entry of a new group/token reference and validate available scope. Use a group picker only if a documented authorized vendor interface supports it; otherwise prompt for the ID.
requirements.acceptance: Missing group/token information requests input; no fabricated group-discovery endpoint is used.

requirements.contract: At acceptance record profile revision, target group and approved inventory revision. A later context/profile change cannot redirect queued jobs or silently change a running action.
requirements.acceptance: Queued/running jobs remain bound to their original approved context or enter explicit reconciliation.

requirements.requirement: Changing selection is not moving a PA
requirements.contract: Switching the group managed by the AI or selecting a profile for a new install does not move, unregister, reinstall or re-register an existing PA. Observed existing agent identity must remain separate from desired configuration.
requirements.acceptance: A context switch causes no target mutation and does not falsely claim the PA belongs to the newly selected group.

requirements.requirement: Moving an existing PA between groups
requirements.contract: If an actual group reassignment is requested, treat it as a separately authorized lifecycle action. Supported vendor procedure, capacity, identity, recovery and qualification remain to be established.
requirements.acceptance: No installed-agent move is offered until the exact procedure and rollback/recovery behavior are qualified.

requirements.contract: Harmony execution-agent routing delivers integration jobs to the shared parent service. Target registration profiles select where target PAs belong; they do not require switching the management dispatcher agent group.
requirements.acceptance: Changing a target registration group does not change its canonical VM destination or introduce per-host round-robin ambiguity.

requirements.contract: Separate valid format, network/access readiness, staged credentials and verified Harmony registration. Prove token/group acceptance with a documented verifier or actual registration evidence.
requirements.acceptance: No generic HTTP success or valid-looking token is presented as authentication/registration proof.

requirements.contract: Create a new profile revision and revalidate affected future actions. Replace target credential files only when explicitly requested and serialized with lifecycle work.
requirements.acceptance: Rotation never overwrites active execution context and does not imply PA reinstall.

requirements.contract: Select management hostname and matching server certificate/private key/required chain, or a declared existing gateway profile. Wizard generates NGINX settings.
requirements.acceptance: Production HTTPS is not published with missing/mismatched/expired required certificate material.

requirements.contract: Keep management server TLS, target server TLS, integration endpoint trust and client mTLS identities separate in discovery, selection, permissions and deployment.
requirements.acceptance: Certificate use matches its purpose; management TLS is not copied into PA integration trust by default.

requirements.contract: Ask for proxy details only where selected/required. Credentials are secret references. Existing proxy qualification is pending.
requirements.acceptance: Unavailable/unqualified proxy flows are shown as blocked, not configured successfully.

requirements.contract: Offer only qualified trust scenarios; existing evidence is scoped endpoint trust and does not establish every custom CA combination.
requirements.acceptance: Selected trust change passes its exact supported tuple and post-change health gate.

requirements.contract: Optional endpoint-specific keys/password references and host fingerprints are separate from management SSH. Existing SSH/SFTP branch is deferred.
requirements.acceptance: Collecting files does not imply implementation; runtime application requires qualification.

requirements.contract: Optional endpoint certificates, private keys/chains/passphrase references require qualification. Do not select server certificates as client identities by filename alone.
requirements.acceptance: Unsupported mTLS application stays blocked and no secret content is echoed.

requirements.contract: Synchronous GET /v1/versions; optional target/action filters. Return governed logical/package releases, platform support, qualification, artifact approval/digest, recommendation and eligibility. Distinct from installed version.
requirements.acceptance: No queue/download/install side effects; unknown context stays unverified; submission revalidates eligibility.

requirements.contract: Expose target listing and proposed named group/profile/file metadata discovery for guided selections, respecting caller scope. Return opaque references, not secrets or arbitrary paths.
requirements.acceptance: Only authorized targets/profiles and valid file candidates are selectable.

requirements.contract: Install/upgrade/uninstall and applicable status/health jobs use fixed approved actions, named targets, idempotency keys and exact release context.
requirements.acceptance: Unsupported input, qualification and artifact approval failures block before execution.

requirements.contract: GET /v1/jobs/{id} reads current persisted state and sanitized result with an evidence reference. Unknown IDs are not assumed pending.
requirements.acceptance: AI clients without polling can retrieve later; no long-running install HTTP connection is held.

requirements.requirement: MCP setup guide options plan and execution
requirements.contract: Proposed getSetupGuide/getSetupOptions/saveSetup/validateSetup/executeSetup tools share the authoritative setup session. getSetupStatus and prepareTarget retain their inspection/preparation roles.
requirements.acceptance: MCP drives onboarding after bootstrap; validation and preparation never implicitly install a PA.

requirements.contract: Jitterbit MCP publishes tools backed by APIM/Studio REST operations. The management service is REST, not automatically a private MCP runtime. No second custom MCP server is a baseline requirement.
requirements.acceptance: Demonstrate actual Jitterbit tool discovery and calls in the licensed tenant.

requirements.contract: Consumes external MCP tools/resources/prompts; does not publish our tools. Use only if a workflow needs another MCP server and endpoint entitlement/version compatibility is verified.
requirements.acceptance: No baseline dependency or false publisher role is introduced.

requirements.contract: Only a selected self-hosted Jitterbit MCP gateway/runtime needs its own environment-scoped control-plane service token. Client authentication tokens are separate.
requirements.acceptance: Hosting choice and vendor packaging are validated; replacement is verified before permanent token deactivation.

requirements.contract: AI-to-MCP, MCP-to-APIM, Studio-to-parent, worker-to-target and PA-to-Harmony identities remain separate. API permissions constrain action/target/profile access.
requirements.acceptance: No registration token substitutes for another scope; unauthorized requests are rejected.

requirements.contract: Record actual Jitterbit/client protocol support and test schemas/error/authentication behavior. Supplied MCP 2026-07-28 documentation does not prove tenant compatibility.
requirements.acceptance: Chosen client discovers and calls tools using a verified supported protocol combination.

requirements.contract: Commit the validated job as READY in management PostgreSQL before returning 202/jobId. The worker claims the persisted backlog directly; no baseline dispatch outbox or queue publication.
requirements.acceptance: Recover lost responses with the same idempotency identity; accepted work survives process restart.

requirements.requirement: JBMQ delivery is outside the simplified baseline
requirements.contract: The earlier outbox/JBMQ/dispatch/ACK path is retained as history. Reintroduce messaging only for a separately justified intake/routing requirement and qualified acceptance contract.
requirements.acceptance: Baseline install needs no outboxId, dispatch API, Studio queue dispatcher or queue acknowledgement.

requirements.contract: Separate worker claims work and canonical host, stages verified JBPA and calls existing lifecycle engine through pinned SSH. No arbitrary shell/SQL tools.
requirements.acceptance: Caller/profile release identities and selected target are pinned and recorded.

requirements.contract: SSH loss, worker crash or lost DB connection can leave remote action active. Retain ownership and inspect original attempt evidence; lease expiry alone does not allow replay.
requirements.acceptance: Interrupted attempts cannot launch a second mutation on the same host.

requirements.contract: Local management bootstrap runs first without an existing management API or MCP dependency. After the stack is running, configure and verify Jitterbit connectivity. MCP-driven executeSetup then creates durable target installation jobs through the existing worker/SSH engine.
requirements.acceptance: Target onboarding and remote JBPA execution work through MCP while retaining idempotency, ownership and recovery guarantees.

requirements.contract: Dedicated Linux/container stack with NGINX, FastAPI/Pydantic/Uvicorn, separate Python worker, PostgreSQL and SQLAlchemy/Alembic. Compose is a recoverable single-host baseline.
requirements.acceptance: Clean supported-host deployment; internal DB/API ports and restricted worker identities.

requirements.contract: Pinned releases/digests, protected profiles, schema migrations, release verification, backups and recovery procedures. No generic downgrade/PA rollback promise.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh deployment, upgrade compatibility and backup restoration are proven.

requirements.contract: Management stack/onboarding remain proposed. Existing JBPA live evidence is scoped; RC9 remote caller/package-changing upgrade/production promotion retain open gates.
requirements.acceptance: Publish support/evidence matrix before production claims.

requirements.contract: Ship tested Studio/APIM/JBMQ/MCP configuration where actual export/import interfaces exist; guided tenant steps where unavailable.
requirements.acceptance: No invented export format or unsupported promise of one-command Harmony provisioning.

requirements.contract: Redundant application/worker hosts and external HA PostgreSQL are optional future profiles; qualify fencing and recovery rather than claiming Compose provides HA.
requirements.acceptance: Prove split-brain protection, shared ownership and recovery before offering HA.

requirements.contract: Agent identity, version, health, capabilities and timestamp; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Locally deployed definitions with qualified IDs/project/environment fields; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Paginated time-bounded PA execution data: operationRunId, operationId where available, operationName, host/agent/group identity, original/normalized status and submitted/started/finished times; duration or current elapsed time with null semantics. Fixed read-only qualified provider, no target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: One PA execution, separate from a definition or management job, with original status, available start/finish timestamps, duration/elapsed time and permitted diagnostics/source metadata; no fabricated missing fields.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Status counts, oldest pending and longest running executions; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: PA component service health; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Local TranDb/PostgreSQL connections, size, waits and bounded statistics; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Jitterbit capacity, request backlog, thread pools and log synchronization; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Bounded checks of approved Harmony/local service endpoints; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Bounded, filtered and redacted component/operation log excerpts; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Host CPU, memory, swap, disk, inode, I/O, network and uptime observations; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Resource observations for permitted PA and supporting processes; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Capability-qualified JVM, Tomcat, Apache, PostgreSQL and PgBouncer metrics; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Installed release/provider/instrumentation support and unavailable reasons; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Time-bounded retained snapshots/aggregations from management-side collection; management-side collection over existing SSH; no added target listener.
requirements.acceptance: Version-qualified provider; source/time/freshness/coverage and unavailable reasons; bounded collection; no baseline regression.

requirements.contract: Optional durable MCP task handles only after verified Jitterbit/client support. Keep parent job persistence and get-job fallback; cancellation does not prove remote termination.
requirements.acceptance: Both endpoints support the extension; safe mapping of job/result/cancellation behavior.

requirements.contract: Stable IDs, scope, agreed/candidate decisions, implementation status, contract, acceptance and source references are canonical JSON; render the repository matrix from it.
requirements.acceptance: IDs unique; every discussion area and deferred tool is present; source links resolve; superseded decisions remain traceable in decisionChanges.

requirements.contract: Use Opportunity Intelligence branding/components. Restructure tables/containers rather than remove them; retain technical detail. Diagrams use aligned blocks, explicit actions, consistent contrast and numbered sequences.
requirements.acceptance: Rendered pages and diagrams reviewed at full size; geometry/pagination checks pass.

requirements.contract: Current PDF v8 precedes the subsequent getVersions/onboarding refinements. Matrix/specification carry current decisions until the HLA is regenerated and visually checked.
requirements.acceptance: Never represent the older PDF as containing later requirements.

requirements.contract: Serve the product-owned guide as an API tool response or verified MCP resource/prompt. Include guide/schema revision, session ID, phases, required fields, file roles, tool names and resumable question rules. No secrets or arbitrary instructions from uploaded files.
requirements.acceptance: Guide and backend schema versions align; uploaded documents cannot redefine authorization or execution.

requirements.contract: Provide an authenticated upload endpoint in APIM/Studio that relays supported file bytes to protected management storage. Return an opaque fileId, validated role and safe metadata. Jobs/JBMQ carry references only.
requirements.acceptance: Verify HTTP v2 default-schema multipart requirements, exact byte/digest preservation, size/type limits, permissions and payload-log exclusions end to end.

requirements.contract: MCP guidance cannot grant filesystem access to the AI. A capable client/uploader sends bytes through the Jitterbit upload API; otherwise provide a private upload page or select files already staged on the management VM. Never paste key content as a default workaround.
requirements.acceptance: Client without file access completes setup by uploading in the private UI or selecting pre-staged files.

requirements.contract: Persist host/profile/file mappings through saveSetup with schema and plan revision. Markdown is instructional content, not an executable script or configuration parser.
requirements.acceptance: Malformed, incomplete, unauthorized and stale file/profile selections are rejected; session can resume.

requirements.requirement: Execute an approved plan through MCP
requirements.contract: executeSetup submits durable work for a validated immutable plan revision and idempotency key. Worker generates/transfers target files and invokes the fixed JBPA installer; returns job references/status.
requirements.acceptance: No direct long-running HTTP install; no arbitrary commands; each host has durable state and reconciliation.

requirements.requirement: Complete management runtime parameters before readiness
requirements.contract: Every required bootstrap setting has a source, validation and consumer: platform/deployment identity, HTTPS/address, API identity/permissions, DB credentials/connection, persistent storage/secrets, releases/artifact policy, worker/recovery limits, network and readiness. Generate safe defaults/secrets rather than asking for every internal field. Target registration/access profiles can follow in MCP onboarding.
requirements.acceptance: A bare VM reaches verified management readiness through the local installer; missing required runtime configuration blocks readiness; MCP configuration occurs afterwards.

requirements.contract: Shared envelope with distinct management-job, operation-definition, operation-run, metric, summary, error and export contracts; unchanged business meanings across MCP/APIM/Studio/REST.
requirements.acceptance: Schema/version validation and opaque ID preservation across all boundaries; no giant all-purpose telemetry payload.

requirements.contract: Bounded cursor pages and permitted host/agent/group/project/operation/status/time filters; deterministic mutable-history snapshot/checkpoint behavior.
requirements.acceptance: Prove no duplicated/lost run records across pages and late finish updates; explicit truncation, stale and query-failure states.

requirements.contract: Separate jobId, operationId and operationRunId; qualify local IDs by source. UTC known times with source metadata; unfinished finishedAt/duration are null and elapsed is separate.
requirements.acceptance: Pending/running/completed/failed records map accurately; absent IDs/times remain unavailable.

requirements.requirement: Summaries and bounded export for AI
requirements.contract: Small summaries/current selections are defaults; detail drilldown and authenticated bounded export references handle larger datasets outside model context.
requirements.acceptance: AI responses stay bounded and scoped; exports/summary windows and coverage are explicit.

requirements.requirement: Incremental collection and retention at scale
requirements.contract: Checkpoint changed/new operation runs and late results; scheduled collection independent of chat; metrics preserve units, types/resets, aggregations, retention and resource limits.
requirements.acceptance: Benchmark load/capacity and recovery; restore checkpoints safely; retain qualified providers and all baseline lifecycle guarantees.

requirements.requirement: Connector readiness independent of core health
requirements.contract: Represent affected connector package availability, runtime load and registry availability separately from PA registration/core/Axis health. Do not claim deploy readiness from HTTP health alone.
requirements.acceptance: A healthy PA with an unavailable adapter reports connector readiness as failed or unverified; targeted evidence identifies the connector without exporting credentials.

requirements.contract: Inspect logical success fields in supported integration responses. HTTP 200 carrying status:false is a failure; preserve safe evidence when the response omits error details.
requirements.acceptance: The recorded invalidation HTTP 200/status:false case cannot be marked successful; no empty outcome list is silently treated as successful processing.

requirements.contract: Guide authorized customers through supported connector update and saved connection testing, then verify actual deployment outcome. Preserve asynchronous download/load state; do not default to reinstall or change credentials.
requirements.acceptance: Recovery records distinguish customer actions, observed download/load events and customer-confirmed deployment from directly captured handler success. Uncertain file-lock/proxy causes remain qualified.

requirements.contract: Validate local secret-file field format before registration, including forbidden control characters and trailing newlines, without logging values. Token validation and group selection are separate from successful Harmony registration.
requirements.acceptance: Malformed single-line protected fields fail before mutation with actionable non-secret guidance; successful registration is verified against the intended group and agent identity.

requirements.contract: Expose pa_assess_operations as one read-only management API/MCP action that selects authorized fixed providers and returns operation/stage/descendant health, findings, evidence and coverage.
requirements.acceptance: A successful root with failed validation children reports FAILED; repeated root runs remain separated; provider timeout returns partial/unavailable rather than healthy.

requirements.contract: Collect redacted curl diagnostic TEXT separately from raw headers/payload. Report configured logging, available traces, interval/caps and exact/inferred/unmatched correlation.
requirements.acceptance: Trace counts are not file totals; rm missing-file messages alone cannot establish business failure; empty logging does not imply no transfers; assessments do not change logging.

requirements.contract: Scope all TranDb reads to permitted target/environment/root/window; aggregate each message/file/summary grain before joining, preserve identity and unknown timing/status semantics.
requirements.acceptance: No join inflation; operation attempts and business-file counts remain separate; status_ts is not falsely projected as finishedAt; missing/failed/truncated sources remain visible.

requirements.contract: Reconcile authorized Harmony/PAG agents with canonical-host inventory and local identities; expose offline, unreachable, uninstrumented, duplicate and unsupported nodes.
requirements.acceptance: Unknown agents/providers cannot be omitted or treated as healthy; group scopes and tenant permissions are enforced.

requirements.contract: Combine interval host/process/pressure measurements with PA services/connectivity, Apache/JVM/Tomcat, TranDb operations/queues/errors/DB and log diagnostics. Return findings, sources, freshness, policy and coverage.
requirements.acceptance: Partial source failures preserve peer results and visible gaps; application validation failures remain distinct from infrastructure saturation.

requirements.contract: Evaluate representative peak history, queue growth, component limits, peers, routing, workload parallelism, downstream/DB capacity, SLOs and N-1 headroom before scale-up/out recommendations.
requirements.acceptance: Idle/short snapshots cannot produce an exact VM SKU or agent count. Idle peers trigger routing/serialization investigation before scale out; missing history yields insufficient evidence.

requirements.requirement: Management-owned historical telemetry and async assessment
requirements.contract: Persist deep fleet read assessments in the existing management durable work model; optional management Alloy textfile/remote-write publishes low-cardinality safe gauges into customer time-series storage.
requirements.acceptance: No added default PA service/port; client polling is optional; metrics include freshness and collection coverage; exporters/native configuration changes are a separately selected profile.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.requirement: Final phase and explicit implementation gate
requirements.contract: Implement skill access hardening last, after selected functional work and only on an explicit user implementation request. Documentation approval does not authorize changing skill/runtime controls.
requirements.acceptance: No code, skill, credentials, SSH or infrastructure changes in this planning update; production remains unavailable until controls are qualified.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Use a dedicated production monitoring identity for bounded reviewed health, metrics, logs and TranDb reads; deny lifecycle and configuration/service mutations.
requirements.acceptance: Monitoring cannot install, upgrade, uninstall, deregister, restart or alter configuration, directly or through a secondary endpoint.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Install, upgrade, uninstall and deregistration require a separate customer-controlled authenticated approval workflow outside the AI session. Destructive production actions require independent two-person approval.
requirements.acceptance: Requester cannot approve their own change; chat confirmation and model-supplied approval flags cannot authorize execution.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Remove production keys, credential-bearing SSH agents, secret-store read/sign access and privileged executor administration from the skill process. Customer-controlled executors obtain scoped credentials.
requirements.acceptance: The AI process cannot read production secrets or invoke their signing authority; tool requests/results and logs exclude credential values.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Separate executors, identities, credentials and privileges for monitoring and lifecycle changes, with environment/customer isolation.
requirements.acceptance: Compromise or misuse of monitoring or QA credentials cannot invoke the production change worker or retrieve its credentials.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Bind approval to customer, environment, host/agent/group, exact action, applicable package digest, plan revision/hash, change window, expiry and execution ID. Revalidate at execution.
requirements.acceptance: Changed, expired, forged or replayed approvals fail; same-job retries reconcile outcomes without repeating uncertain mutations.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Resolve allowlisted target IDs through trusted inventory; authenticate the requester and enforce customer/environment/action authorization.
requirements.acceptance: Arbitrary IPs, caller-defined QA labels, identities or role fields cannot redirect execution or bypass production policy.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Use root-owned reviewed collectors and forced-command wrappers with strict arguments and narrowly scoped sudo. Do not expose general shell, Python/script uploads, arbitrary SQL or paths.
requirements.acceptance: Command/script/SQL/path injection, writable-wrapper substitution and shell escalation are denied; no additional target service or listening port is required.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Support dedicated executor-held keys, short-lived customer-CA certificates or enterprise PAM; cloud management-plane adapters require separate qualification. Pin host identity and restrict forwarding/PTY.
requirements.acceptance: Credentials are environment/role scoped with issuance, rotation and revocation evidence; expiry is not claimed to terminate existing sessions.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.requirement: Local uninstall and Harmony deregistration are separate
requirements.contract: Expose local uninstall and Harmony record deregistration as distinct actions with separate target evidence, approval and outcome records.
requirements.acceptance: Uninstall approval never implicitly authorizes Harmony record deletion; deregistration cannot affect a different agent/group.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Recheck target state/identity, applicable drain conditions, capacity and maintenance policy immediately before execution; serialize per host and hold uncertain outcomes for reconciliation.
requirements.acceptance: Missing policy/identity/evidence blocks mutation; fresh install checks host/group and known agent state rather than requiring an existing agent ID.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Record requester, approvers, policy decision, plan hash, safe credential references and execution outcome in an independently protected audit destination. Provide operator-only mutation/issuance disable controls.
requirements.acceptance: AI cannot approve, alter audit records/policy or disable the kill switch; already-running actions follow explicit reconciliation rather than assumed cancellation.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.contract: Return bounded allowlisted diagnostics; customer controls raw evidence and approved AI data handling. Logs, Markdown and tool output cannot redefine permissions or actions.
requirements.acceptance: Secrets/payloads are excluded by default; malicious log instructions cannot promote monitoring to lifecycle privileges.

requirements.area: Deferred skill access and production security
requirements.requirement: Production security qualification and safe rollback
requirements.contract: Qualify the skill broker and target restrictions in QA/canary before production. Test forbidden monitoring actions, all bypass routes, approval abuse, policy outage and interrupted execution; obtain security sign-off.
requirements.acceptance: Negative tests demonstrate independent enforcement; rollback disables production access and never restores unrestricted workstation production SSH.

requirements.contract: JBPA invokes the default vendor package upgrade and observes; it does not disable autostart, restart from verification or alter vendor deployment/configuration.
requirements.acceptance: Vendor starts once; JBPA observer issues no start/stop/restart or deployment/configuration writes.

requirements.contract: Require fresh runtime/identity evidence, complete vendor-expanded Axis files and valid conversion WSDL in addition to core service/connectivity checks.
requirements.acceptance: Slow startup is polled; incomplete/corrupt expansion or an HTTP 200 error page prevents upgrade success.

requirements.contract: Route requested older releases through qualified complete uninstall/fresh reinstall. Pin and preflight the target artifact/resources before removal, preserve requested evidence and report registration/slot consequences.
requirements.acceptance: No silent in-place downgrade or automatic Harmony deletion; failed preflight leaves the current agent installed.
